Definition:
Autonomous AI agents that use an LLM to decide what to do next

Eg: multi-step reasoning, tool use, planning, and decision-making with durable state across long-running interactions.

Note:
- Agents can run in an Activity: usually shorter-running, less valuable agent runs. Produces fewer Actions.

- Agents can run in the Workflow: each incremental step of the agent's action is recorded in Temporal Event History. These use a lot of Actions, but are worth if for complex agents that create real economic value.
Example Customers / Patterns: Codex, Lindy (AI assistants), Anthropic (Agents API), Retool (AI workflows), Gorgias (AI support agents), Dust, Lovable AI, Scale AI
AE Litmus Test (Question to ask yourself: Does an LLM decide what to do next (plan, choose tools/steps), across a multi-step workflow?
Volume proxy: User interactions or API calls per month triggering an agentic loop

Example Customers / Patterns: Block/K-Goose (agentic platform), Stripe, Coupang, enterprise platform teams
AE Litmus Test (Question to ask yourself: Are they building a platform for many Agents that other internal teams can plug in to?

Definition:
Fixed, code-defined pipelines that support or serve AI inference. 

A few types:

- AI Workflows: content or media generation, deep research (fan out/ fan in)

- Context prep: document processing (eg, parsing end-user-uploaded PDFs), temp file management, preparing and refreshing a corpus of knowledge an AI system will access at query/inference-time

- Retrieval: search and surfacing of information in a corpus (eg, using the parsed data from end-user-uploaded PDFs to answer a specific query)
Example Customers / Patterns: Harvey (legal doc analysis), EvenUp (demand letters), Juristat (patent processing), Hebbia (document AI), Descript (media transformation), Washington Post (perceptual AI), Netflix Plato (media workflows), Abridge (medical transcription), ZoomInfo (RAG/GenAI summaries), DataStax (durable RAG), Baseten (inference serving), Messari (crypto research AI)
AE Litmus Test (Question to ask yourself: Is the workflow a fixed pipeline that runs data through AI models (RAG, doc/media processing, inference, classification)?
Volume proxy: AI API calls or batch pipeline runs per month triggering a linear pipeline (embed → retrieve → generate → store)

Definition:
Training, fine-tuning, and experiment orchestration workflows that update model weights 

Eg: training runs, hyperparameter sweeps, RLVF (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards), distributed training coordination, and MLOps pipelines.

RLVF requires a tremendous amount of compute and therefore orchestration goes towards this because it is yielding such powerful model improvements. You define a goal and let the LLM try so solve it billions/ trillions of times
Example Customers / Patterns: Anthropic (model training), Coupang (ML platform), NVIDIA (training orchestration), Bridgewater (ML workflows)
AE Litmus Test (Question to ask yourself: Is the workflow orchestrating training or fine-tuning that updates model weights (runs, sweeps, RLVF)?
Volume proxy: Training jobs or experiments per month; blend data pipeline (12 actions/run) for data prep + infra automation (18 actions/run)

Definition: Deployment pipelines, infrastructure provisioning, release automation, configuration management, and platform engineering workflows.
Example Customers / Patterns: DataDog, Netflix/Spinnaker, Cloudflare, Nutanix, Equinix, HashiCorp, Anthropic (infra/security), Block (deploy platform rebuild), Humana

Is the primary outcome shipping or operating infrastructure/software (deploy, provision, upgrade, rotate, rollback) reliably?

Unsure if the use case might actually be control plane operations? If it’s deploy/provision/upgrade/operate, pick this one

Definition:
Managing the full lifecycle of domain entities 
Eg: subscriptions, accounts, resources, sessions, or any long-lived object with state transitions over time.
Example Customers / Patterns: Yum! Brands (menu versioning), Vodafone (CPE management), Workday (employee lifecycle), Anthropic (sandboxes lifecycle), Turo, ANZ (mortgage lifecycle)
AE Litmus Test (Question to ask yourself: Is the workflow managing a long-lived “thing” over time (account, subscription, resource, session, case)?
Volume proxy: Active entity population (customers, accounts, assets, subscriptions); multiply by interaction rate: ~5 signals + 20 queries + 3 activities + 1 timer per entity per month
